local.title: Spring work waits for **firm ground.**
local.intro: In Flint Township, a spring cleanup starts when you can walk the lawn without leaving tracks. Much of the ground here drains slowly, so yards stay soft well after the snow melts.

points.title: Ruts turn into bumps
points.body: Wheel ruts and footprints in wet soil harden into bumps you mow over all summer. We do the beds and the debris first and hold the first cut until the lawn can carry a mower.

points.title: Sticks and brush
points.body: Winter brings branches down. Emterra takes bundled brush no thicker than 2 inches and no longer than 4 feet, and not from contractors, so what our crew picks up goes in our trailer.

points.title: Pickup starts in April
points.body: Township compost pickup starts the first Thursday in April. A cleanup in late March does not have to wait for it, because our debris never goes to the curb anyway.

points.title: Leave the lilacs for later
points.body: MSU Extension says spring flowering shrubs set their buds the summer before, so cutting them in spring cuts off the flowers. During a cleanup we take out dead and broken wood and leave the shaping of lilac and forsythia until after they bloom.

logistics.title: How a spring cleanup runs in Flint Township.
body: Rob walks the yard with you and notes what winter left behind: sticks, matted leaves along the fence, beds that need cutting back, edges that have grown over. He quotes the cleanup, and fresh mulch can be added to the same job.

On the day the crew picks up debris, rakes out matted leaves, cuts back last year's perennials, cleans and edges the beds and blows off the drive and walks. The first cut happens when the lawn is firm enough to take it.
Once the beds are clean, see [mulch and flower beds](/mulch-and-flower-beds/) for colors and depth, and [weekly mowing in Flint Township](/lawn-mowing-flint-township-mi/) for the rest of the season.

faq.q: Do you do spring cleanups in Flint Township?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes does spring cleanups in Flint Township: winter debris and sticks out, matted leaves raked up, beds cleaned and edged, perennials cut back and the first cut done. Rob quotes it free.

faq.q: When should spring cleanup be done in Michigan?
faq.a: Once the snow is gone and the ground is firm enough to walk on without sinking. In Genesee County that is often April, and later on wet, heavy soil. Beds and debris can go first, and the first cut waits for the lawn to firm up.

faq.q: Should I trim my shrubs in the spring?
faq.a: Dead and broken wood, yes. MSU Extension says spring flowering shrubs like lilac and forsythia are pruned right after they bloom, because their flower buds formed the summer before. Summer bloomers can be pruned in late winter or early spring.

faq.q: Will the township pick up my yard waste in spring?
faq.a: From the first Thursday in April, yes. Emterra's weekly compost pickup takes brown yard waste bags, X marked cans and bundled branches up to 2 inches thick and 4 feet long. Material from a contractor is not accepted, so our cleanup debris leaves with us.
